recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the Security work group wants new substantive Provenance import guidance, or if IHE publication links move again and need separate link maintenance.
issue_request: FHIR-20623 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Security issue asking the Provenance import section to point readers to the IHE QEDm Provenance profile as an exemplar for importing FHIR resources derived from document-sharing infrastructure. The accepted resolution was to narratively point the existing Import section at IHE QEDm and the RECON profile, with no clear need for more text.
initial_application: The Jira comment links HL7/fhir PR #708. Local git history shows commit b569c4406b1d2a7944cc4b25869f7075524fe4f3, "Provenance and general security CR", adding the Import anchor and the IHE QEDm/RECON example list to source/provenance/provenance-notes.xml on 2019-10-03. Although that commit did not name FHIR-20623, it matches the Jira-linked PR, timing, artifact, and requested narrative content.
additional_context: Provenance is active in source/fhir.ini, and current source/provenance/provenance-notes.xml already says examples of this Provenance-profile activity can be found in IHE Implementation Guides for QEDm and RECON. A later FHIR-36234 reconcile commit, 5c7c4a06170e72255199e88f0a1bd476fad55ff8, updated those old IHE wiki URLs to formal IHE publication locations. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later or conflicting decision for FHIR-20623.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source already satisfies the approved narrow narrative-pointer resolution, and adding more local prose or a new core profile reference would exceed that decision.

related_jiras.note: A separate Published technical correction replaced the QEDm and RECON IHE wiki URLs with formal IHE publication links while preserving the FHIR-20623 narrative pointer.
